standard.title: Method for Sampling Green Coffee in Bags (हरी कॉफ़ी के थैलों से नमूने लेने की विधि)
standard.description: This standard specifies a method of sampling a consignment of green coffee in bags, shipped as a part of a lot, containing 10 bags or more, for the purpose of drawing representative increments and preparing laboratory samples for contract verification, quality control, arbitration, and laboratory testing.
standard.scope: This standard specifies a method of sampling a consignment of green coffee in bags, shipped as a part of a lot, containing 10 bags or more, for the purpose of drawing representative increments and preparing laboratory samples for contract verification, quality control, arbitration, and laboratory testing.

certification.description: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 10814 is a statistical sampling methodology rather than a direct physical consumer product, it does not carry an individual mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product stamp on its own. However, compliance with its sampling scales, trier extraction methods, and sample-handling timelines is strictly integrated into national export audits, state crop-procurement contracts (including Coffee Board of India auctions), and legally binding quality agreements between global trade buyers and processors across India.
requirements: The sampling method applies to consignments or lots shipped in ten (10) bags or more. Lots are presumed to be of roughly uniform character.
Each elementary increment extracted from a single bag must be exactly 30 g ± 6 g of green coffee beans.

Requires the use of a metal coffee trier (conforming to ISO 6666) to draw increments through the bag wall. This puncture method avoids opening the bags, as the woven fabric naturally closes after extraction.
All elementary increments drawn from the selected bags must be aggregated in a clean, dry, odor-free container to form a unified global bulk sample of at least 1500 g.

Requires preparing at least three representative laboratory samples of at least 300 g each from the mixed global sample. One sample is for the buyer, one for the seller, and one is held as a reference sample for arbitration.
Samples intended for moisture analysis or water-sensitive tests must be packed in clean, dry, hermetically sealed, airtight containers and filled as completely as possible.

Sampling must be performed by trained personnel, and a written report must be prepared noting: damaged/sweated bags in the lot, environmental and storage conditions, date/time, and any notable observations.

Observed or calculated weights, percentages, and bag calculations must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained must be identical to the specified limit.
